notes: Identity assessment: supplied PMC full-article parse names Matthew Baldwin and Joris Lammers, title Past-focused environmental comparisons promote proenvironmental outcomes for conservatives, PNAS 113(52), 14953–14957 (2016), DOI 10.1073/pnas.1610834113; these match the neutral original reference. This is a primary research report containing Methods and Results, SI Methods and Results, Discussion and references, rather than only an abstract. No PDF is supplied; page 3 cannot be visually checked. The primary report identity is confirmed, but the supplied study identifier 8 has no corresponding study heading. The broad description and p.3 locator do not distinguish message liking, environmental attitudes, behavior, simple slopes, interactions, or meta-analysis. Multiple printed b coefficients fit the broad description. No coefficient can be assigned without an unsupported mapping; do not equate the eighth enumerated study with study 8. Candidate evidence only, not assigned values: Study 1 message-liking interaction b = 0.42, SE = 0.11, t(199) = 3.71, P < 0.001; Study 1 environmental-attitudes interaction b = 0.19, SE = 0.08, t(199) = 2.25, P = 0.03; Study 2 conservative linear condition effect b = 0.37, SE = 0.14, t(258) = 2.71, P = 0.007; Study 3 environmental-attitudes interaction b = 0.008, SE = 0.004, t(196) = 2.22, P = 0.03. These retain printed b labels; no standardisation identity inferred and no conversion performed. Study 7 is explicitly a meta-analysis and prints modifier β = 0.64, SE = 0.26, z = 2.47, P = 0.01; it is not identified as the assigned target. Only es_value_o is assigned; all other statistic fields, replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders, not assessments of source availability or prior verified values.
